subject: math

objective.text: Solve multi-step addition word problems with tape diagrams. Check answers by rounding.

explanations.title: Tape for each quantity
explanations.text: Draw one tape for each quantity. If one quantity is more than another, extend its tape by the extra amount.

explanations.title: Multi-step problems
explanations.text: Find the missing quantity first. Then find the total. Use a letter for the unknown.

explanations.title: Estimate first
explanations.text: Before you solve, round each number to get a general sense of the answer. After you solve, compare the answer with the estimate.

explanations.title: Reasonable answers
explanations.text: An answer is reasonable if it is close to the estimate. If it is not close, check your work.

explanations.title: Smaller units are closer
explanations.text: Rounding to a smaller unit gives an estimate closer to the actual answer. Rounding to a larger unit has a larger margin of error.

examples.text: 14,594 pink roses. 14,594 plus 7,857 is 22,451 red roses. 14,594 plus 22,451 is R. R is 37,045.

examples.title: Bus tickets over the weekend

questions.text: Big Bill's sold 118,214 pairs of boots. They sold 37,092 more pairs of sandals than boots. How many pairs of sandals did they sell?
Big Bill's sold 118,214 pairs of boots. They sold 124,417 more pairs of sneakers than boots. How many pairs of sneakers did they sell?
Big Bill's sold 118,214 boots, 155,306 sandals and 242,631 sneakers. How many pairs of footwear did they sell in all?
Connie baked 144 cookies. Esther baked 49 more than Connie. How many cookies did Esther bake?
Round 144 and 193 to the nearest ten. Add them. What is the estimate of the cookies?

The estimate is 330 and the exact answer is 337. Is the answer reasonable?

questions.text: Week 1 had 10,827 cans. Week 2 had 1,256 more cans than week 1. How many cans were collected in week 2?
The four weeks had 10,827, 12,083, 10,522 and 20,011 cans. How many cans were collected in all?
Round the four weeks to the nearest thousand and add: 10,827, 12,083, 10,522 and 20,011. What is the estimate?
Scott earned 8,999 dollars in January. In February he earned 2,387 dollars more. How much did he earn in February?
Scott earned the same in March as in February. He earned 8,999, 11,386 and 11,386 dollars. How much did he earn in all?
Round Scott's three months to the nearest thousand and add: 8,999, 11,386 and 11,386. What is the estimate?
The estimate is 31,000 and the exact answer is 31,771. Is the answer reasonable?

questions.text: The school website had 9,854 hits in February. January had 3,905 more hits than February. How many hits did it have in January?
January had 13,759 hits and February had 9,854. Round each to the nearest thousand and add. What is the estimate?
January had 13,759 hits and February had 9,854. How many hits did the website have in both months?
The estimate is 24,000 and the exact answer is 23,613. Is the answer reasonable?
77,098 fans went to the Jets game. 3,397 more fans went to the Giants game. How many fans went to the Giants game?
77,098 fans went to the Jets game and 80,495 to the Giants game. How many fans went to both games?
Round 77,098 and 80,495 to the nearest thousand and add. What is the estimate?
Buttercup made 7,087 liters of milk. Betsy made 986 more than Buttercup. How many liters did Betsy make?
Daisy made 5,098 liters, Betsy 8,073, Mary 9,980 and Buttercup 7,087. How many liters did all four cows make?
Round the cows' milk to the nearest thousand: 5,098, 8,073, 9,980 and 7,087. Add them. What is the estimate?
The estimate is 30,000 and the exact answer is 30,238. Is the answer reasonable?

hints.text: Say the digit and its place. Then say its value.
Find the two units around the number. Compare with the halfway point.
Line up the places. Add from the right. Regroup when you have 10 of a unit.
Find the missing quantity first. Add the extra amount to the quantity you know.
Add the quantities on all the tapes to find the total.
Round each number to the named place. Then add.
Compare the exact answer with the estimate. Are they close?
Find the missing quantity first. Then add everything.

assets_required.why_this_method: The lesson uses tape diagrams drawn on paper. The child cannot draw them.
assets_required.description: A vertical addition with place value columns up to hundred thousands and a tape diagram. The child adds, regroups, and compares the sum with a rounded estimate.
must_show_exactly: Columns in order: hundred thousands, ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, ones
Two or more addends stacked with places lined up
A row for the regrouped 1 above the next column
A tape diagram with two or three tapes, a bracket and a variable for the total
An estimate box beside the exact answer
states_or_frames: A column with 10 or more regrouped
Sum complete and compared with the estimate
assets_required.interaction: Child adds one column at a time and sees regrouping. The child enters an estimate and the widget shows if the sum is close.
assets_required.alt_text: A vertical addition problem with regrouping, a tape diagram and an estimate box.
assets_required.generation_caption: A clean vertical addition with six labeled columns, carry marks, a tape diagram beside it and an estimate box. [Build by code]
